title: DLF — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
According to reviews on MouthShut, some customers have expressed dissatisfaction with DLF Group, citing issues such as non-refundable shift charges, poor customer service, and delays in project completion. On BBB, DLF Law Group, LLC has received numerous complaints, with reviewers describing the company as unprofessional, accusing it of harassment, and reporting issues with debt collection. While some reviews mention positive aspects, the majority highlight significant problems.

DLF Real Estate has faced significant reputation problems and criticism. According to reviews on MouthShut, buyers have expressed frustration over delayed projects, lack of concern for buyer pain, and high non-refundable charges. The DLF Story by Aditya Grover highlights several controversies, including the IPO non-disclosures, the Vadra land grab case, a CCI penalty for abusing a dominant position, and a QIP non-disclosure controversy. Additionally, MantrA SmS Alert notes that DLF struggled with debt and declining profits, leading to project exits and a leaner business structure by mid-2010.

My take: I do feel that here again, the concept of materiality must be kept in mind as an investor of DLF. The amount of Rs 50 Cr that Mr. Vadra gained from this case is irrelevant, the real concern is the negative image that DLF has been dealing with since it became a political issue in 2012. The practice of land allocation to developers through bidding and lottery systems by district development authorities [...] It wasn't just one isolated controversial incident involving DLF; rather, the period from its IPO in 2006 was marked by numerous controversies for India's largest real estate giant. Here are some key cases I plan to discuss:

> 1. DLF IPO Controversy around Non-disclosures in DRHP (2006)
> 2. DLF - Vadra Land Grab Case (2008)
> 3. CCI penalty of Rs 630 Cr for abusing ‘Dominant Position’ (2011)
> 4. QIP Non-disclosure controversy (2019) [...] All in all, I do feel DLF did get a bit unlucky. It was the only player who got punished by CCI out of 70 others (as reported by ET). Its IPO controversy started in 2007 and continued to tarnish its reputation till 2015 when SAT overturned SEBI’s order. A small deal with Mr. Robert Vadra caught national headlines on a daily basis as political parties continued to attack them for years and whatnot.
